subject.statement: Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty to a money laundering charge and served four years in prison.

summary: Verdict: FALSE at 25% confidence. While Changpeng Zhao did plead guilty to a money laundering charge (violating the Bank Secrecy Act), he served only a four‑month prison sentence, was released on 2024‑09‑27, received a pardon in October 2025, and a UK High Court civil claim remained active as of July 2026. The claim that he served approximately four years in prison is therefore incorrect.

findings.statement: Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty to violating the Bank Secrecy Act, a money laundering charge.
Changpeng Zhao was sentenced to four months in prison, not approximately four years.
The exact length of Changpeng Zhao's prison sentence was four months.
Changpeng Zhao was released from custody on September 27, 2024.
Changpeng Zhao received a presidential pardon from Donald Trump in October 2025.
As of July 2026, a UK High Court claim filed by nearly 1,700 British investors against Binance and Changpeng Zhao remains ongoing, indicating the pardon did not extinguish civil liability.

conflicts: Are there any ongoing legal proceedings or appeals related to his guilty plea? - supported by 99bitcoins.com, financemagnates.com, wsj.com (weight 1.65) vs refuted by gov.ca.gov (weight 0.95)
conflict_notes: Q8 Are there any ongoing legal proceedings or appeals related to his guilty plea?: supporting sources (99bitcoins.com, financemagnates.com, wsj.com) weight 1.65 vs refuting source (gov.ca.gov) weight 0.95. The supporting sources refer to a civil UK High Court claim, while the refuting source concerns criminal proceedings; the pardon would resolve criminal liability but does not affect the civil claim, so the claim of ongoing legal proceedings (civil) is weighed as true.
